# Scanpath Studio

> Free, open-source software for visualizing eye-tracking data from reading studies: scanpaths, fixations, saccades, gaze heatmaps and raw gaze drawn over the text, from EyeLink, Tobii and other eye trackers.

Scanpath Studio is an interactive Streamlit workbench, a Python API (`import scanpath_studio as sps`) and a CLI (`scanpath-studio`) for eye-tracking-while-reading data: it draws fixations, saccades and heatmaps over the text at its true on-screen position, shows the per-word reading measures your data brings (FFD, FPRT, RPD, TFD, skips, regressions), compares participants, and exports figures and tables. The bundled demo is a subset of the OneStop Eye Movements corpus.

# Use the app

# Get started

## Install

- **Desktop app** Recommended

  No coding required. Your data stays on your computer.

  [macOS](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-macos-arm64.dmg) [Windows](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-windows-x86_64-setup.exe) [Linux](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-linux-x86_64.tar.gz)

  Setup details & other downloads

  - macOS 14+, Apple silicon: open the DMG, drag to Applications, then launch. If blocked: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. Intel Mac or older macOS? Use Python below.
  - Windows: run the installer, then launch from Start. If SmartScreen warns: More info → Run anyway. A [portable ZIP](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-windows-x86_64.zip) is also available.
  - Linux: extract, then run `./ScanpathStudio/ScanpathStudio`.

  [All downloads](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest)

- **Try online**

  Explore the bundled demo. No installation.

  [Launch demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app)

- **Install with Python**

  Python 3.11–3.14. Opens in your browser.

  ```
  pip install scanpath-studio
  scanpath-studio
  ```

## Your first figure

Start with the bundled [OneStop sample](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#onestop). No files to prepare: choose a look and save an interactive figure.

\[!\[

\](../assets/workflows/design-presets_poster.webp)\](../assets/workflows/design-presets.mp4)

- **1 · Open a reading**

  In Scanpath, keep **Bundled demo** selected. Use **Select trial** to choose a reading.

- **2 · Choose a view**

  Click **Heatmap** in Design presets to see where fixation time concentrates. Switch to **Scanpath** to follow the sequence.

- **3 · Save your figure**

  Open **Export → Current figure**, choose **HTML**, then download. Open the saved file to explore the figure in your browser.

- **[Bring your own data](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data)**

  Import your recordings and check the column mapping.

- **[Prepare a figure](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-one-figure/index.md)**

  Choose a format and size for your paper or slides.

- **[Explore more views](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)**

  Try an example, then follow its app instructions or the [feature guides](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/index.md).

- **[Work in code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/#render-in-code)**

  Reproduce a view in Python or with the CLI.

# Analyze a corpus

- **[Analyze one text](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/analyze-one-text/index.md)**

  Compare word-by-word measures across readers.

- **[Compare groups or conditions](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/compare-groups/index.md)**

  Inspect group means and differences.

- **[See progression over time](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/progression-over-time/index.md)**

  Inspect trends within or across trials.

## Before you start

Open a dataset and set the trial filters for your question. Word-level views need [reading measures in the Words table](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#reading-measures); the bundled demo includes them. For comparisons across readers, the same text must have the same text ID.

## Keep the result

Download this table (CSV) saves the values. Download the recipe (JSON) saves the dataset name, filters, analysis choices and counts. Keep the source data separately so the result can be reproduced.

To draw a summary with Python or the CLI, see [Plot a summary in code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/corpus-workspace/#plot-a-summary-in-code).

# Analyze one text

Compare how participants read the words of one text.

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start), then open Corpus Analysis → Per text.
1. Pick a text and an available reading measure.
1. Choose a word profile on the stimulus or a plot against a word feature, such as surprisal if that column is present.
1. Set the aggregation, spread and minimum participants per word. Check the counts before interpreting differences.
1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/corpus-analysis_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/corpus-analysis.mp4)

*The recording shows total fixation duration on a text, against GPT-2 surprisal, and between two groups.*

# Compare groups or conditions

Compare a reading measure between two cohorts.

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start), then open Corpus Analysis → Groups.
1. Turn on Compare a second group.
1. Split a field or define independent filters for the two groups.
1. Choose Group means & difference and a measure. Check the number of participants in each group and any overlap. A standardized difference is shown only for non-overlapping groups.
1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

The comparison is descriptive; it does not run a significance test. For a recorded example, see [Analyze one text](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/analyze-one-text/index.md).

# See progression over time

Inspect a measure within trials or across a session.

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start) and open Corpus Analysis.

1. Choose the view for the question:

   | Scope                                                       | View                                          |
   | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
   | One participant across trials                               | Per participant → Per-trial trend             |
   | Fixation duration within trials, pooled for one participant | Per participant → Fixation duration over time |
   | A group across trials                                       | Groups → Group trend                          |

1. Choose a measure and aggregation where offered. For across-trial trends, map the recorded trial-order column when importing; inferred order may differ from presentation order. For the within-trial view, choose fixation order or recorded onset time if available.

1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

# Optimize data collection

- **[Check a session](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/index.md)**

  Inspect a pilot or completed recording.

- **[Compare two eye trackers](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/compare-eye-trackers/index.md)**

  Review recordings of the same text.

- **[Audit an experimenter](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/audit-an-experimenter/index.md)**

  Review sessions by who collected them.

Start with a [loaded dataset](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data). To apply exclusion decisions after reviewing, use [Filter data](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/index.md).

# Audit an experimenter

Review recordings collected by one experimenter.

1. Keep an experimenter field when importing the data, or attach it in a participants table if each participant has one experimenter.
1. Open the filter button beside Select trial and choose the experimenter. Participants-table fields appear under By participant.
1. [Inspect and replay their trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#2-inspect-a-trial).
1. Tag trials `review` in Annotations and note recurring observations.
1. [Export the review](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#5-save-the-review).

To compare experimenters, turn on Compare, filter each scanpath's trial list by a different experimenter, and select readings of the same text.

# Check a session

Inspect a recording and save the trials that need attention.

## 1. Open the session

[Import your tables](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data), or select a loaded dataset. Check its Recording setup against the screen used in the experiment.

## 2. Inspect a trial

Select a participant and trial in Scanpath. Turn on Word boxes and inspect:

- whether the boxes match the stimulus screenshot, if available;
- how fixations sit relative to the words;
- unexpected gaps, shifts or off-screen positions.

For a consistent offset, check [coordinate units and screen setup](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/faq/#the-fixations-dont-line-up-with-the-text).

## 3. Replay the recording

Turn on Animate to inspect fixation order and timing. To mark short, long or out-of-bounds fixations, use Plot controls → Filters & highlights → Fixations and choose Highlight. Gaps and unusual scanpaths alone do not establish their cause.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/replay_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/replay.mp4)

## 4. Record the review

In Annotations, tag a trial `review` and note what you observed. Use the trial picker's arrows to continue through the session.

## 5. Save the review

Export stars, tags and notes from Data Management → Annotations → Export. The record includes participant and trial IDs. Use Open on an annotation row to return to that trial.

For exclusion decisions, follow [Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md).

# Compare two eye trackers

Review the same text recorded with two trackers or setups.

1. [Import each recording](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data) as a separate dataset with its own Recording setup.
1. Open the first dataset and select a trial in Scanpath.
1. Turn on Compare. In scanpath B's row, choose Dataset B and a trial of the same text.
1. Compare fixation placement, spread and missing stretches. Use side-by-side views for different screen sizes; an overlay requires matching screen coordinates.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/compare_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/compare.mp4)

*This recording compares two readers in the demo. For two trackers, select the second recording under Dataset B.*

Use [the session-review steps](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#4-record-the-review) to save observations.

# Filter data

- **[Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md)**

  Leave tagged trials out.

- **[Select participants by a field](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/select-participants/index.md)**

  Use participant metadata.

- **[Find the trials an analysis needs](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/find-trials-for-an-analysis/index.md)**

  Select trials after inspecting fixations.

## Before you start

Open a dataset in Scanpath. The filter button beside Select trial selects whole trials. Plot controls → Filters & highlights changes which fixations and saccades the figure draws.

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/trial-filtering_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/trial-filtering.mp4)

## Check and export the selection

1. Check the remaining trial and participant counts and inspect a few trials.
1. Follow [Export every trial](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-every-trial/index.md), choosing the active filtered pool. The bundle's `index.csv` lists its files and trial IDs.
1. Keep a full decision record with [Data Management → Annotations → Export](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#5-save-the-review). Bundle annotations cover only the exported trials.

# Exclude unsuitable trials

Apply your exclusion criteria and leave rejected trials out of the selection.

1. [Review the session](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#2-inspect-a-trial). Judge trials against your study's criteria; a scanpath pattern alone does not establish skimming or poor calibration.
1. In Annotations, tag rejected trials `exclude` and add a brief reason.
1. Open the filter button beside Select trial. Under By trial annotation, enter `exclude` in Excluding tags.
1. [Check and export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

For trials with several screens, apply the exclusion tag to the whole trial. A screen-only annotation does not exclude its parent trial.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/favorites_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/favorites.mp4)

*The recording shows stars and tags. Use the `exclude` tag and Excluding tags for the selection above.*

# Find the trials an analysis needs

Locate trials containing particular fixation patterns.

1. Open Plot controls → Filters & highlights → Fixations.

1. Set the relevant category to Highlight:

   - Short or Long, with a duration threshold in milliseconds
   - Out of bounds, for fixations outside every word box
   - Blink, if your data includes a blink column

1. Step through the trials. In Annotations, tag those that meet your analysis criteria, for example `include`.

1. Open the filter button beside Select trial. Under By trial annotation, enter `include` in With any of these tags.

1. [Check and export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

# Select participants by a field

Select readers using metadata such as native language, age or group.

1. Attach a table with one row per participant and a participant ID column: use Metadata → Participants when adding a dataset, or Data Management → Edit dataset → Data tables & column mapping afterwards.
1. Open the filter button beside Select trial, then By participant.
1. Choose a field and the values or range to keep.
1. Check the remaining participant IDs and [export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

To also apply trial-level quality criteria, follow [Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md).

# Export customized figures

- **[Export one figure](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-one-figure/index.md)**

  A static image or interactive HTML.

- **[Export a replay](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-a-replay/index.md)**

  GIF, MP4 or interactive HTML.

- **[Export every trial](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-every-trial/index.md)**

  A ZIP of figures and data tables.

For installation requirements or a failed export, see the [export FAQ](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/faq/#export-fails).

# Export a replay

Save an animated reading for a talk or supplement.

1. Select a trial in Scanpath and turn on Animate.
1. Set the playback speed and visible layers.
1. Open Export → Current figure and choose GIF, MP4 or HTML.
1. Download the replay. GIF and MP4 use the selected playback speed; HTML has interactive playback controls.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/replay-export_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/replay-export.mp4)

*Exporting a GIF; the rendering wait is shortened in this recording.*

For [GIF/MP4 export from Python](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/#replays-as-gif-or-mp4), see Export and share.

# Export every trial

Build a ZIP of static figures and data tables for a set of trials.

1. [Set the figure's design](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-one-figure/#1-choose-the-view) once. Each exported trial uses that design, without animation or a comparison partner.
1. Open Export → Export bundle and select this trial, the active filtered pool, or the whole dataset.
1. Choose figure and table formats and check the filename pattern. For editing individual layers later, enable separable layers.
1. Build and download the bundle, then inspect one exported figure.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/export-bundle_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/export-bundle.mp4)

*Exporting figures and tables for the demo's trials; the build is fast-forwarded.*

Keep `plot_config.json` for the design, `README.md` for the build details and `index.csv` for the file list and failures. Keep your original data and record its version and the selected trial filters separately.

For a [scripted batch](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/#batch-pattern), use the Python recipe in Export and share.

# Export one figure

Save a scanpath, heatmap or comparison at the size you need.

## 1. Choose the view

Select a trial in Scanpath. Choose a design preset or adjust the layers in Plot controls. Turn on Compare if the figure needs two readings. Check that text and markers are readable and nothing is clipped.

## 2. Set the format and size

Open Export → Current figure.

| Output             | Format     |
| ------------------ | ---------- |
| Image              | PNG        |
| Vector figure      | SVG or PDF |
| Interactive figure | HTML       |

For a print PNG, set Width and DPI. For HTML that opens offline, tick Self-contained HTML.

## 3. Download

Use the download button for the chosen format.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/export-figure_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/export-figure.mp4)

*Exporting a PNG at 180 mm and 300 dpi.*

## 4. Reuse the design or share the figure

- My designs in Plot controls saves the look for other trials.
- Share → Link reopens the trial and settings; uploaded data must be loaded separately.
- [Share → Code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/#from-the-app-to-a-script) gives Python or CLI code to redraw the figure.
- Share → File saves the settings to load again.
