# Corpus Analysis

Summarize reading measures by text, participant or group. The selected dataset and trial filters apply here too.

## Choose a view

| View            | Use it to                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Per text        | Compare word-by-word reading across participants |
| Per participant | Inspect one participant across trials            |
| Groups          | Compare conditions or populations                |

Choose a measure, aggregation and spread. For word profiles, set the minimum number of participants per word.

## Supply reading measures

Word-level analyses use the [reading measures in your data](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#reading-measures), such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map those columns when importing. Fixation views use the fixation table.

## Compare groups

Split on a field or define cohorts with filters. Turn on Compare a second group to see group means and their difference. These comparisons are descriptive.

## Save results

Download a result table as CSV and its analysis recipe as JSON. The recipe records the dataset, filters and analysis choices. Return to Scanpath to inspect individual trials.

## Plot a summary in code

Use a tidy summary table: a word profile needs `word_id` and `value`, with optional `lo` and `hi` for a band. Rename a source word ID column to `word_id` if needed. Use a result table exported from Corpus Analysis. For a trial-order trend, see [Across the experiment](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/across-experiment/index.md).

Python and CLI: word profile

```
import pandas as pd
import scanpath_studio as sps

profile = pd.read_csv("profile.csv")
fig = sps.plot_corpus_figure(
    profile, kind="profile", measure_label="Total fixation duration (ms)"
)
sps.save_figure(fig, "profile.html")
```

```
scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile \
  --measure-label "Total fixation duration (ms)" -o profile.html
```

[API parameters](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/api/#scanpath_studio.api.plot_corpus_figure) · [CLI options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cli/#corpus)

# Export and share

Save a figure, export a batch, or reuse a view in the app or in code.

## In the app

| Goal                                | Where                       |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Save the figure or replay on screen | Export → Current figure     |
| Export many trials and their tables | Export → Export bundle      |
| Share a view or copy its code       | Share → Link or Code        |
| Reuse the design                    | My designs, or Share → File |

For step-by-step instructions, see the [export tutorials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/index.md).

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/share-link_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/share-link.mp4)

A shared link reopens the view for someone with the same dataset loaded.

## Reproduce a figure

Open Share → Code and copy Python or CLI. The snippet carries the figure's settings and your column mapping; replace any placeholder file paths. [Render in code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/#render-in-code) shows a minimal example.

For a print-sized PNG, Python's `save_figure` accepts `width_mm` and `dpi`; the CLI uses `--width-mm` and `--dpi`. Use `save_figure_layers` or `render --separable-layers` for editable layers.

## Batch export

Export → Export bundle uses the chosen trials in the app. For a scripted batch, loop over the trial list:

Python: one HTML figure per trial

```
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
out = Path("figures")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for pid, tid in sps.list_trials(words, fixations).itertuples(index=False):
    fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid)
    sps.save_figure(fig, out / f"{pid}_{tid}.html")
```

Use the [data loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#load-and-inspect-in-code) for your own files. The CLI's `render` writes one trial per invocation.

## Replay export

With Animate on, Export → Current figure saves HTML, GIF or MP4. The CLI's `render --animate` saves interactive HTML. For a GIF or MP4 in Python:

Python: save a GIF or MP4

```
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps
from scanpath_studio.animation_export import export_animation

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
replay = sps.animate_scanpath(words, fixations, "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele_r0")
Path("replay.mp4").write_bytes(export_animation(replay, fmt="mp4"))
```

Use `fmt="gif"` and a `.gif` filename for GIF output.

[Export setup and troubleshooting](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/faq/#export-fails) · [Python save options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/api/#save) · [CLI options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cli/#common-tasks)

# Data management

Load your own data, open a public corpus, or try the bundled sample.

## Choose a dataset

Use the dataset picker or the Data Management page:

- Bundled demo: a small OneStop sample
- Hand-drawn sample: a six-word trial
- Public corpora: OneStop and PoTeC, downloaded on your computer
- - → Import files: your own tables
- - → Create manually: type text and place fixations

### OneStop

The demo comes from [OneStop Eye Movements](https://github.com/lacclab/OneStop-Eye-Movements) (Berzak et al., 2025), an English corpus with 360 participants. The full corpus is available as four datasets: ordinary reading, information seeking, and their repeated-reading versions. Each downloads once from [OSF](https://osf.io/2prdq/).

## What your data needs

At least one of the first three tables below; add others as needed.

| Table                  | Contents                                                       |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fixations              | One row per fixation: trial ID, duration, and x/y or a word ID |
| Words (interest areas) | One row per word: trial ID, word ID and bounding box           |
| Raw gaze               | One row per sample: participant ID, trial ID, x and y          |
| Participants           | One row per participant, with metadata                         |
| Trials                 | One row per trial, with metadata                               |
| Texts                  | One row per text, with metadata                                |

Columns are detected from common eye-tracker exports; check and correct the mapping when importing. Keep condition labels and other columns with Extra fields to keep. Metadata fields are available for filtering, sorting and grouping.

### Files and units

- CSV, TSV, TXT, Parquet, Feather, Excel, or a ZIP of these files
- Positions in pixels
- Times in milliseconds; headers marked `[s]` or `[μs]` are converted
- Word boxes as `x/y/width/height` or EyeLink's `IA_LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM`

### Trials over several screens

Map `screen_id` in your tables, and `screen_index` for their order if needed. The app displays one screen at a time.

### Reading measures

Include per-word reading measures in the Words table, such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. EyeLink's `IA_*` columns are detected. Corpus Analysis uses the measures you supply.

## Add your own data

1. Choose + → Import files and name the dataset.
1. Upload your tables and check the column mapping.
1. Enter the recording screen size and typography where known.
1. Optionally attach stimulus screenshots from a local folder.
1. Click Add dataset.

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/add-your-data_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/add-your-data.mp4)

## Load and inspect in code

Load the same files in a script; column names are detected automatically.

Python and CLI

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_scanpath_data("ia.csv", "fixations.csv")
print(sps.list_trials(words, fixations))
```

```
scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --list-trials
scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv
```

For raw gaze, metadata and explicit column mappings, see the [loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/api/#load-your-data) and [CLI input options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cli/#render).

## Manage datasets

Click a dataset row to open it. Inspect its tables, annotations and data checks below the list.

Use Edit dataset to change its name, column mapping, recording setup or metadata, then Save changes. Download setup file saves the mapping and recording setup for reuse.

Only imported columns are available in the editor. To use a column left out at import, add the files again.

# Scanpath visualization

1. Views and Help.
1. The trial control bar: dataset, trial, screen, sort (⇅) and filter ().
1. The trial's summary.
1. The figure.
1. Plot controls.
1. Annotations, Stimulus & context, Comparisons, Export and Share.

The Scanpath view draws one reading on the screen it was recorded on.

Looking for a specific button?

[All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md) lists every button and setting on this view, menu by menu, with a picture of each menu. Search it for what you want to change, such as *saccade color* or *legend position*.

## Choose a trial

Pick a trial above the plot. The filter () beside it narrows the list by text, participant, condition or annotation, and **⇅** sorts it. A trial with several screens gets a second navigator to move between them. When several participants have the same trial ID, each reading is in the list on its own, with its participant in brackets, `3 [p2]`.

## Control the layers

The **Plot controls** column holds every setting of the figure. Each layer is one line: a switch, and a **▾** with its settings.

| Section              | What it controls                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Animate              | play the reading as a video, at a speed you choose                                                                   |
| Compare              | a second reading beside or over this one                                                                             |
| Design presets       | restyle the whole figure in one click: Scanpath, Heatmap, Illustration or your last custom settings                  |
| My designs           | save the current settings as a design, apply it again in one click, or export it to share or use on another computer |
| Palette              | one color scheme for the whole figure, such as colorblind-safe or print                                              |
| Fixations            | markers: size, color, order                                                                                          |
| Saccades             | lines and arrows, colored by direction or reading type                                                               |
| Stimulus             | text, span highlight, stimulus image, font and background                                                            |
| Word boxes           | each word's interest area: outline and fill, color and opacity                                                       |
| Heatmap              | where fixations concentrate, by count or duration                                                                    |
| Raw gaze             | the gaze samples as recorded                                                                                         |
| Filters & highlights | which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out                                                          |
| Figure & canvas      | screen framing, axes and grid, title and labels, hover fields, legends                                               |

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/plot-controls_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/plot-controls.mp4)

## Under the plot

| Tab                    | What it is for                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Annotations**        | Star, tag and write notes on the trial, to find or filter it later.                                                                                   |
| **Stimulus & context** | The trial's context, such as its title, question and answers, and its highlighted word spans.                                                         |
| **Comparisons**        | Compare this trial with other trials that match it on a field you choose, such as other readings of the same text, shown side by side.                |
| **Export**             | Download the figure (PNG, SVG, PDF, HTML) or the video (HTML, GIF, MP4), or a zip bundle of figures and data for many trials.                         |
| **Share**              | A link that reopens this view (for whoever has the same dataset loaded), the Python or command-line code that redraws the figure, or a settings file. |

Watch the tabs under the figure

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/subtabs_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/subtabs.mp4)

## Render in code

Set up a figure in the app, then open Share → Code for its Python or CLI recipe. For uploaded data, replace the placeholder file paths with your own.

Python and CLI: render the demo

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele_r0")
sps.save_figure(fig, "scanpath.html")
```

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele_r0 -o scanpath.html
```

For your own files, use the [data loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#load-and-inspect-in-code). Figure settings are listed in the [API options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/figure-options/index.md) and [CLI options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cli/#common-tasks).

The [gallery](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md) gives app, CLI and Python instructions for heatmaps, comparisons, replays and other views. For [batch exports and GIF/MP4](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/index.md), see Export and share.

## Back up your work

Each of these files can be saved and loaded again:

| What                               | Where                                      |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| figure settings                    | **Share → File**                           |
| favorites, tags and notes          | **Data Management → Annotations → Export** |
| column mapping and recording setup | **Edit dataset → Download setup file**     |
| saved figure designs               | **My designs → Export**                    |

None of them holds your data, so load the same data before restoring one. On your own computer, the app also keeps your datasets and work between sessions.

# All controls

Every control on the **Scanpath** page, where it is and what it does — in the order you meet them on screen. Search this page (`Ctrl`+`F`, or `Cmd`+`F` on a Mac) for the thing you want to change, such as *colors*, *legends* or *axes*.

The page has two sets of controls:

- The **trial control bar**, above the plot, decides *what* you see: the dataset, the trial, and which trials are in the list.
- The **plot controls**, the column on the right, decide *how* it is drawn: each layer of the figure, its colors and sizes, and the figure as a whole.

The tabs under the plot then work with the trial on screen: annotate it, read its context, compare it, export it or share it. For how the parts fit together, see the [Scanpath visualization](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/index.md) guide.

For the corresponding Python keywords and CLI flags, use the [figure options table](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/figure-options/index.md).

## Trial control bar

The bar above the plot: pick a dataset and a trial, step through the trials, and narrow, sort or label the list.

| Control                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Select dataset**                                | The dataset the page shows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **+** → **Create manually**                       | Add a dataset by manual illustration: write a text and place its fixations by hand.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **+** → **Import files**                          | Add a dataset from data tables: upload your own tables as a new dataset.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Select trial**                                  | The trial to show. Click it and type to narrow the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Trial** slider                                  | Scrub through the trials in the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **◀ ▶**                                           | The previous or next trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **⇅** → **Sort trials by**                        | Reorder the trial list by a statistic (such as reading time), a participant, text or condition field, or a column of a metadata table you attached.                                                                                                                       |
| **⇅** → **Descending**                            | Reverse that order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| → **Text** / **Participant**                      | Keep only these texts or participants.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| → *a field of your data*                          | Keep only trials with these values, or, for a number, in this range.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| → **By participant** / **By trial** / **By text** | The same, for the columns of an attached metadata table.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| → **Favorites only**                              | Keep only starred trials.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| → **With any of these tags**                      | Keep only trials with any of these tags.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| → **Excluding tags**                              | Hide trials with any of these tags, such as `exclude`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| → **Clear all filters**                           | Reset every filter in the panel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **✏️** → **Show chips above the plot**            | Show or hide the row of facts about the trial above the plot.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **✏️** → field lists                              | Drag fields between *Shown* and *Available* to choose the chips. *Available* holds every field with one value per trial: participant, text and condition columns, the columns of any metadata table you attached, and statistics such as reading time and fixation count. |
| **✏️** → field colors                             | Give a chip a highlight color; its **✕** puts it back to the default gray.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **✏️** → **Refresh fields**                       | Look again for which fields are trial-level.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Screen** and its **◀ ▶**                        | On a trial recorded over several screens: the screen to show.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## Plot controls

The column on the right of the plot. At the top, the modes and designs change the whole figure at once. Under them, each layer of the figure has a row of its own: the switch turns the layer on or off, and the **▾** beside it opens that layer's settings, described below one menu at a time. The last two rows, **Filters & highlights** and **Figure & canvas**, cover the figure as a whole. A greyed-out control says why when you hover over it.

### Animate: play the reading as a video

The **Animate** switch turns the figure into an animation, a video of the reading played back fixation by fixation, with play and pause buttons and a time slider under the plot. Its **▾** holds:

| Control                                 | What it does                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Replay** → **Speed**                  | How fast the video plays, from ×0.25 to ×8: ×1 is the reader's own pace, ×2 twice as fast, ×0.5 half as fast.            |
| **Replay** → **Autoplay** → **On load** | Start playing the animation automatically as soon as the plot is shown; otherwise it starts only when you click play.    |
| **Replay** → **Duration**               | For information only: the trial's reading time, and how long the video runs at this speed.                               |
| **Frames** → **Quality**                | How smooth the video is: more frames play more smoothly but take longer to build. **Custom** sets the two below by hand. |
| **Frames** → **Every**                  | Reading time between frames, in ms.                                                                                      |
| **Frames** → **Limit**                  | The most frames a video gets; a long trial gets wider frame steps to fit.                                                |
| **Frames** → **Result**                 | For information only: how many frames this trial's video has, and how far apart they ended up.                           |

### Compare

The **Compare** switch shows a second scanpath, B, beside or over this one (pick it in the [trial control bar](#trial-control-bar), above the plot); its **▾** holds:

| Control                         | What it does                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **View**                        | **Overlay** both scanpaths, or give each its own panel, **Side by side** or **Top & bottom**.                     |
| **Stimulus from**               | In an overlay, whose word boxes and text are drawn: both, A's or B's.                                             |
| **Label A** / **Label B**       | Each scanpath's name in the legend, written with fields such as `{participant_id}`; empty uses the automatic one. |
| **Available fields**            | The fields a label can use.                                                                                       |
| **Step** → **A and B together** | ◀ ▶ move both scanpaths at once.                                                                                  |

### Design presets and palette

Restyle the whole figure in one click, with a ready-made design or one of your own saved designs:

| Control                                       | What it does                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Scanpath** / **Heatmap** / **Illustration** | Ready-made designs: a classic scanpath, a word-box heatmap, or a clean schematic.                                                                                            |
| **Custom**                                    | Your most recent hand-made settings.                                                                                                                                         |
| **My designs**                                | Your saved designs: click one to apply it; the pencil renames it and the bin deletes it.                                                                                     |
| **My designs** → save button                  | Save the settings on screen as a named design, to apply again later in one click.                                                                                            |
| **My designs** → **Export** / **Import**      | Download your designs as a file, or load a file of designs: share a look with co-authors and partners, reproduce a figure exactly, or move your designs to another computer. |
| **Palette**                                   | A color scheme for the whole figure, such as colorblind-safe or print.                                                                                                       |

### Fixations

The **Fixations** switch draws the fixation markers; its **▾** holds:

| Control                                                                     | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Marker** → **Color**                                                      | What decides each marker's color. **One color** paints them all alike. Pick a number column of the fixations, such as duration or the fixation's order in the trial, and the markers follow a color scale: with the default blues, longer fixations show darker. Pick a category, such as the line of text or the next saccade's direction, and each value gets its own color, with a legend. |
| **Marker** → color box                                                      | Choose the fixation marker color.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Marker** → **Shape**                                                      | Choose the fixation marker shape: circle, square, diamond, triangle, star…                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Marker** → **Size**                                                       | Set the marker size range: the smallest and largest marker diameter, in px.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Marker** → **Scale**                                                      | Choose how duration sets marker size: square root, linear, log, or relative to the trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Marker** → **Durations**                                                  | Choose the duration range: set the durations that get the smallest and the largest marker.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Marker** → **Opacity**                                                    | Set the fixation marker opacity; lower it to see overlapping fixations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Marker** → **Outline**                                                    | Set the width and color of the ring round each marker.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Color bar** → **Show**                                                    | Show the color scale's bar, when markers are colored by a number.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Color bar** → orientation, **Angle**, **Size**, **Thickness**, **Length** | Set the bar's direction, tick-label angle and size, and its thickness and length.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Fixation index** → **Show**                                               | Number each fixation in reading order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Fixation index** → color, **Size**                                        | Choose the numbers' color and size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Snap** → **To line**                                                      | Move each fixation onto its line of text — a schematic, labelled *Illustration*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Snap** → **Position**                                                     | Choose where on its line a snapped fixation sits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

### Saccades

The **Saccades** switch draws the lines between fixations; its **▾** holds:

| Control                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Line** → **Color**                  | Choose what decides the saccade color: one color for all; forward saccades and regressions in two colors; or a color per saccade type (forward, skip, refixation, return sweep, regression), with a legend. Forward / regression and by type need a word ID for each fixation, the word it landed on, mapped in your fixations table (such as EyeLink's `CURRENT_FIX_INTEREST_AREA_ID`); without one every saccade reads as *other*. |
| **Line** → color box                  | Choose the saccade line color.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Line** → type colors                | With **By type**: choose the color of each saccade type, such as regressions or return sweeps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Line** → **Style**                  | Choose the saccade line style: solid, dashed, dotted or dash-dot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Line** → **Width**                  | Set the saccade line width (thickness), in px.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Line** → **Opacity**                | Set the saccade line and arrow opacity; lower it to bring the fixations forward.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Shape**                             | Choose the saccade shape: straight lines, or arcs over the text (a schematic, labelled *Illustration*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Direction arrows** → **Show**       | Show saccade direction arrows: an arrowhead on each saccade, pointing where the eye went.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Direction arrows** → **Arrow size** | Set the saccade arrowhead size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

### Stimulus

The **Stimulus** switch draws the text and the stimulus image; its **▾** holds:

| Control                                | What it does                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Text** → **Show**                    | Show the stimulus text, the words the participant read, at their place on the screen.                |
| **Fit** → **Fit to word boxes**        | Size the stimulus text to fill its word boxes, instead of a fixed font size.                         |
| **Spacing**                            | Set the stimulus text line spacing: how far apart the lines are, in font sizes.                      |
| **Size**                               | Set the stimulus text font size, in px or pt.                                                        |
| **Font**                               | Choose the stimulus text font (typeface); *Other…* takes any font name.                              |
| **Color** → text color                 | Choose the stimulus text color.                                                                      |
| **Background**                         | Choose the plot background color: a preset, or any color in the box beside it.                       |
| **Highlight** → **Show**               | Highlight words in the stimulus text, such as the answer span.                                       |
| **Highlight** → **Highlight words by** | Choose which words to highlight: a true/false word column, such as the critical span.                |
| **Style**                              | Choose the word highlight style: colored text, or a border round the words; and the highlight color. |
| **Image** → **Show**                   | Show the stimulus image, the screen as shown in the experiment, under the scanpath.                  |
| **File**                               | Upload a stimulus image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) to draw under the scanpath.                         |
| **Opacity**                            | Set the stimulus image opacity; lower it so the scanpath reads over it.                              |
| **Offset** → **X** / **Y**             | Move (nudge) the stimulus image left, right, up or down, in px, to line it up with the word boxes.   |
| **Scale**                              | Resize (scale) the stimulus image so its text matches the word boxes.                                |

### Word boxes

The **Word boxes** switch draws each word's interest area; its **▾** holds:

| Control                    | What it does                                            |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Box** → **Line** color   | Choose the word box outline (border) color.             |
| **Box** → **Line** opacity | Set the word box outline opacity; 0 hides the outlines. |
| **Box** → **Fill** color   | Choose the word box fill color, inside each box.        |
| **Box** → **Fill** opacity | Set the word box fill opacity; 0 draws outlines only.   |

### Heatmap

The **Heatmap** switch shows where reading concentrated; its **▾** holds:

| Control                                                                               | What it does                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Style**                                                                             | Choose the heatmap style: colored word boxes, a smooth interpolated map, or fixation density.                                         |
| **Blur**                                                                              | Set the heatmap blur: how far each fixation spreads, for the smooth styles; **Auto** picks it.                                        |
| **Color** → **By**                                                                    | Choose what the heatmap measures: total fixation duration (dwell time), or the number of fixations.                                   |
| **Color** → **Colors**                                                                | Choose the heatmap colors (color scale).                                                                                              |
| **Scale**                                                                             | Choose a linear or log heatmap scale.                                                                                                 |
| **Range**                                                                             | For word-box heatmaps, fix the color range across trials. **Auto** fits each trial. Interpolated heatmaps use each figure's own peak. |
| **Opacity**                                                                           | Set the heatmap opacity; **Auto** uses each style's own.                                                                              |
| **Color bar** → **Show**, orientation, **Angle**, **Size**, **Thickness**, **Length** | Show the heatmap color bar, and set its orientation, label angle and size, thickness and length.                                      |

### Raw gaze

The **Raw gaze** switch draws the gaze samples as recorded; its **▾** holds:

| Control                  | What it does                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| **Marker** → **Color**   | Choose the raw gaze sample color.    |
| **Marker** → **Size**    | Set the raw gaze sample marker size. |
| **Marker** → **Opacity** | Set the raw gaze sample opacity.     |

### Filters & highlights

Which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out:

| Control                         | What it does                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Fixations** → **Index range** | Show only some fixations: a range of the reading order, such as fixations 10 to 40.                                                           |
| **Fixations** → **All trials**  | Keep that fixation range when you move to another trial; otherwise it applies to this trial only, and the next trial shows all its fixations. |
| **Short** / **Long**            | Find short or long fixations by a duration threshold (ms): **Highlight** marks them, **Discard** hides them.                                  |
| **Out of bounds**               | Highlight or discard out-of-bounds fixations, which land in no word box.                                                                      |
| **Blink**                       | Highlight or discard fixations at or next to a blink (needs a blink column).                                                                  |
| marker and color                | Choose the marker shape and color of each highlighted fixation kind.                                                                          |
| **Saccades** → **Types**        | Show only some saccade types, such as regressions or return sweeps. Needs a word ID for each fixation, as for coloring saccades by type.      |

### Figure & canvas

The figure as a whole:

| Control                                       | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Frame** → **Crop to data**                  | Crop (zoom) the figure to the part of the screen with data, instead of the whole screen.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Margin**                                    | Set the crop margin: the space round the data when cropping; **Auto** uses 5%.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Border** → **Show**, color                  | Show the border line round the plot area, and choose its color. It marks the edge of the screen, or, with **Crop to data**, the edge of the cropped area.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Grid** → **Show**                           | Show pixel grid lines (a coordinate grid) over the screen.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Grid** → **Auto**, interval                 | Set the grid spacing (interval), in px, or let **Auto** choose it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Labels**                                    | Set the grid label (tick label) font size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Axes** → **X** / **Y**                      | Choose the x and y axis fields. **X** / **Y** draws the reading on the screen. Any other pair turns the figure into a scatter plot (chart) of the fixations, with no text, word boxes or saccades, keeping the marker colors and sizes. For example: **Time (ms)** against **X** for a time course of the reading, where regressions show as dips; **Time (ms)** against **Word #** for reading progress through the text; **Fixation #** against **Duration (ms)** for fixation durations over the trial. |
| **Illustration** → **Label**                  | Choose when to label the figure as a manual illustration, not the recorded positions: when a setting changes its geometry (such as snapping fixations to a line or drawing saccades as arcs), always, or never.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Illustration** → **Text**                   | Write the *Illustration* label's text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Title** → **Show**, text, **Size**          | Add a figure title above the plot, and set its font size; `{field}` inserts a value of the trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Caption** → **Show**, text, **Size**, color | Add a figure caption below the plot, and set its font size and color.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Hover** → **Words** / **Fixations**         | Choose the hover fields: what the tooltip shows when the mouse is over a word or a fixation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Legends** → **Show**                        | Show or hide each legend: Compare (A/B), Saccade types, Fixation colors, Size key or Text highlight.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Legends** → **Position**                    | Choose the legend position: a corner, the middle of an edge, or down a side, outside or inside the plot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Legends** → **Arrangement**                 | Choose the legend arrangement: items stacked or side by side.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Legends** → **Text size**                   | Set the legend text (font) size, in px.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Reset visualization

The button at the foot of the column.

| Control                 | What it does                                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Reset visualization** | Reset all plot settings to the defaults. Annotations, filters, data and the selected trial stay. |

## In Compare

With **Compare** on, scanpath B gets a row of its own, and several menus split into a **Scanpath A** and a **Scanpath B** group.

| Control                                                                 | What it does                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Dataset B**                                                           | Choose the dataset scanpath B comes from: this one, or another dataset.                                                                                                           |
| **Trial B**, slider, **◀ ▶**                                            | Choose scanpath B's trial: 📄 marks the same text, 👤 the same participant.                                                                                                       |
| **⇅** on B's row                                                        | Sort scanpath B's trial list, apart from A's. By default, trials of the same text as A come first, then the same participant, then the rest; or sort by any field, as on A's row. |
| on B's row                                                              | Filter scanpath B's trials, apart from A's.                                                                                                                                       |
| **Fixations ▾** → **Scanpath A / B** → **Color**, **Size**, **Opacity** | Choose each scanpath's fixation marker color, size range and opacity.                                                                                                             |
| **Saccades ▾** → **Scanpath A / B** → **Color**, **Style**, **Width**   | Choose each scanpath's saccade line color, style and width.                                                                                                                       |
| **Word boxes ▾** → **Scanpath A / B** → **Line**, **Fill**              | Choose each scanpath's word box outline and fill colors and opacities.                                                                                                            |
| **Heatmap ▾** → **Scanpath A / B** → **Colors**                         | Choose each scanpath's heatmap colors (color scale).                                                                                                                              |
| **Raw gaze ▾** → **Scanpath A / B** → **Color**                         | Choose each scanpath's raw gaze sample color.                                                                                                                                     |
| **Filters & highlights ▾** → **· B** groups                             | Set scanpath B's own fixation range, fixation highlights and saccade types.                                                                                                       |

## Under the plot

The tabs under the figure:

| Tab                    | Control                                                 | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Annotations**        | **Favorite**                                            | Star the trial as a favorite, to find it again with the favorites filter.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                        | **Tags** / **Add a tag**                                | Tag the trial, with an existing tag or a new one, such as `exclude`. Tags let you filter the trial list later: the in the trial control bar keeps or hides trials by tag.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                        | **Notes**                                               | Write a free-text note on the trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

|                        | **Highlighted spans**                                   | Choose true/false word columns to highlight in the text, each with a summary.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

|                        | **Columns**                                             | Set how many comparison panels per row.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

|                        | **Formats** / **Tabular data**                          | Choose the bundle's figure formats and the data tables (CSV or Parquet) to include.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                        | **Separable layers**                                    | Export each visual layer (fixations, saccades, word boxes…) as its own file, to stack in a vector editor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                        | **Annotations (JSON)** / **Settings file (JSON)**       | **Settings file**: beside each trial's figure, a `plot_config.json` recording how it was drawn (layers, colors, sizes, screen, title and caption), so the figures are documented. **Annotations**: one `annotations.json` with the exported trials' favorites, tags and notes, which **Data Management** → **Annotations** can import again.                                                                                                                               |

The bundled demo works anywhere; a public corpus has to be downloaded on their side; for your own dataset, send its files and setup file ( **Edit dataset** → **Download setup file**) so they can add it first. A link made on your own computer (a `localhost` address) opens only where the app runs at that same address. |
|                        | **Code** → **Flavour**, **Show every option**           | Get the Python or command-line code that redraws this figure, for scripts and reproduction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
